ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a single-phase full-bridge VSI. The left bridge leg consists of upper transistor Q1 and lower transistor Q4, and the right bridge leg consists of upper transistor Q3 and lower transistor Q2; beside each IGBT there is a corresponding anti-parallel diode D1, D4, D3, D2. The DC power supply Vdc is connected between the upper and lower DC buses. The midpoints of the two bridge legs serve as the AC output terminals, and the right side is connected to a series R-L load; the figure marks the positive and negative polarity of the output voltage vo, as well as the reference direction of the load current io flowing rightward through inductor L and resistor R. Reasoning: The problem states that this VSI supplies a 50 Hz square-wave output voltage to an R-L load with R=3 Ω and L=55.9 mH. Because the load contains a relatively large inductance, when the output voltage commutates, the load current cannot change abruptly and will maintain its original direction for a period of time. Therefore, in the initial stage after voltage reversal, the current first freewheels through the corresponding anti-parallel diodes, rather than immediately flowing through the newly triggered IGBTs. The new group of IGBTs can be turned on by applying gate signals while their current is still zero, until the load current naturally crosses zero and then transfers from the diodes to the IGBTs. Therefore the suitable soft-switching transition is that the IGBT realizes zero-current switching at turn-on.

method.method_draft: First identify from the image the H-bridge legs, the antiparallel diodes, and the R-L load current reference. From the text note that the output voltage is a 50 Hz square wave applied to an R-L load. Since the load is inductive, at every voltage reversal the load current keeps its old direction and initially flows through the antiparallel diodes rather than through the newly gated IGBTs. The new IGBTs can be turned on while their current is still zero, and current transfers to them only at the natural zero crossing. Conclude that the appropriate transition is ZCS during turn-on.

图像描述：附图显示一个单相全桥VSI。左桥臂由上管Q1和下管Q4组成，右桥臂由上管Q3和下管Q2组成；每个IGBT旁都有对应的反并联二极管D1、D4、D3、D2。直流电源Vdc接在上下直流母线之间。两个桥臂中点作为交流输出端，右侧连接串联R-L负载；图中标出了输出电压vo的正负极性，以及负载电流io向右流过电感L和电阻R的参考方向。
推理：题目说明该VSI给R=3 Ω、L=55.9 mH的R-L负载提供50 Hz方波输出电压。由于负载含有较大电感，输出电压换向时负载电流不能突变，会保持原方向一段时间。因此在电压反向后的初始阶段，电流先通过相应的反并联二极管续流，而不是立即流过新触发的IGBT。新一组IGBT可以在其电流仍为零时加门极信号导通，直到负载电流自然过零后才由二极管转移到IGBT。因此合适的软开关过渡是IGBT在 turn-on 时实现零电流开关。

method.method_draft: First read from the image that the VSI is a full bridge supplying an R-L load through the leg midpoints, with diodes D1-D4 available for freewheeling/regeneration paths. From the text take f = 50 Hz, so T/2 = 10 ms, and R = 3 ohm, L = 55.9 mH. Compute the load time constant tau = L/R ≈ 18.6 ms, which is larger than the half-cycle scale, so current cannot reverse immediately at a voltage transition. If desired, solve the half-cycle response: the periodic current crosses zero only several milliseconds after the voltage reversal. Therefore, immediately after a commanded transition the load current is carried by antiparallel diodes and the newly gated IGBTs carry zero current; when they start conducting, the current is zero. Image description: The attached circuit diagram shows a voltage-source inverter full bridge with four IGBTs labeled Q1, Q3 on the upper positions and Q4, Q2 on the lower positions. Each IGBT has an antiparallel diode labeled D1-D4. A DC source Vdc feeds the bridge. The R-L load is connected between the two bridge leg midpoints, and the output voltage vo polarity and load current io direction are indicated at the load.

Reasoning: The output is a 50 Hz square wave, so the period is T = 20 ms and each voltage half-cycle lasts T/2 = 10 ms. The load values are R = 3 Ω and L = 55.9 mH, giving the load time constant tau = L/R = 55.9 mH / 3 Ω ≈ 18.6 ms. Since tau is larger than the 10 ms half-cycle, the inductor current cannot reverse instantly when the inverter output voltage reverses. Thus, immediately after a commanded transition from one bridge diagonal to the other, the load current still has its previous direction and is naturally carried through the antiparallel diodes rather than immediately through the newly gated IGBTs. In the periodic square-wave response, the current crosses zero only several milliseconds after the voltage reversal, so the newly turned-on IGBTs begin to conduct when the current reaches zero. Therefore the suitable soft-switching transition is zero-current switching during turn-on.
